n: A wise child listens to a parent’s discipline; a scoffer refuses to listen to correction.
Good words bring good things back to the speaker, but treacherous people crave violence.
Guarding your words guards your life; speaking rashly brings ruin.

f.w: He that keepeth his mouth keepeth his life

n: The lazy person wants things but gets nothing; the diligent are fully satisfied. Wishing is not the same as working.
The righteous hate lies; the wicked act shamefully and bring disgrace.
Righteousness guards the person of integrity, but wickedness brings down the sinner.
Appearances deceive: some pretend to be rich but have nothing; others seem poor but have great wealth. Jesus warned about being rich in things but poor toward God.

f.w: maketh himself poor, yet hath great riches

n: A rich man may need to pay a ransom to save his life, but a poor man doesn’t even hear threats. Wealth can make you a target.

f.g: Doesn’t hear threats—no one bothers to threaten him.

n: The light of the righteous shines brightly, but the lamp of the wicked will be snuffed out.

f.w: the lamp of the wicked shall be put out

n: Pride produces only quarrels; wisdom belongs to those who take advice.
Quick, dishonest wealth dwindles; wealth gathered little by little grows.

f.g: vanity = emptiness; here, quick or dishonest means.

f.w: he that gathereth by labour shall increase

n: Waiting endlessly for something you hope for can make the heart sick, but a fulfilled longing is like a tree of life. An honest picture of emotional experience.

f.w: Hope deferred maketh the heart sick

n: Whoever scorns instruction pays for it; whoever respects a command is rewarded.
The teaching of the wise is a fountain of life that helps a person escape death’s traps.
Good sense wins favor, but the way of the unfaithful is rough and leads to ruin.

f.w: the way of transgressors is hard

n: Prudent people act with knowledge; fools put their foolishness on display.

f.g: Spreads it out like goods on a market stall.

n: An untrustworthy messenger causes trouble, but a faithful envoy brings healing.

f.g: An envoy, someone sent with a message.

n: Rejecting discipline leads to poverty and disgrace; accepting correction brings honor.
A fulfilled desire is sweet, but fools refuse to turn from evil even to get what they want.
Choose your friends carefully: you become like those you spend time with.

f.w: He that walketh with wise men shall be wise

n: Trouble chases sinners, while good things come to the righteous.
A good person leaves a legacy for grandchildren. Wealth gathered by sinners often ends up in the hands of the righteous.

f.w: an inheritance to his children's children

n: A poor person’s field can produce plenty of food, but injustice sweeps it away. The poor are often harmed by unfair systems, not just bad luck.

Loving parents discipline their children diligently; failing to correct a child is not kindness. The “rod” stood for discipline; modern readers should apply this with the love and gentleness the gospel teaches.

f.g: betimes = early, diligently, in good time.

f.w: He that spareth his rod hateth his son

n: The righteous have enough to eat, but the wicked go hungry.

f.w: to the satisfying of his soul
